brief_rationale: The doctor correctly framed the episode around renal/anticoagulant risks, used the clinical workspace to ground incomplete data, screened symptoms and red flags, advised against self-adjustment of cardiovascular medications, and delivered a layered executable follow-up plan with clear emergency triggers and a family teach-back. However, the doctor prematurely committed to a specific antibiotic recommendation (phosphomycin) and dosage before confirming the final urine culture report, true eGFR, and drug sensitivity, which constitutes a serious in-chain error that forces grade 1 (unsafe). This error also supersedes any high-order credit.
